1.plain: Three sides sit past the 80° valve — Iran 82° (cooling a degree as the corridor track gains a UAE contact and a date), US 84°, Saudi–UAE 84°. The Small Gulf's mechanical score reads 71° (6.2) — below the valve since this morning, because its Sep 4 Kuwait hit aged out of the 7-day window — whether that counts as the pot cooling below the valve is held for Sam's tick under the approval gate. Nobody is near 100° (capitulation).
1.trade: Brent bid but fading on the Oman track; 30-yr yield bid; Polymarket 'Iran–Oman agreement by Sep 30' at 30% is the line to watch into Monday.

2.plain: The door is shut, the bypass too: 3 big ships a day on PortWatch (week to Sep 6); 7 in / 16 out of all sizes on AIS in the 24 h to 17:53 UTC Saturday with 27 ships in the strait — one VLCC-class hull is still the only big crude cargo of the week; CENTCOM says it has turned 100 ships in 60 days and let 'ZERO' through; the East-West pipeline to Yanbu is stopped 'as a precaution', Iraq has shut three or four crossings with Iran, and US air cover for tankers on the Omani lane is down to two time slots a day.
2.trade: Each week under 10 transits/day has lifted Brent; creditor selling steepens the curve.

3.plain: Carriers hold outside Iran's 300 km ring; the fight is inside it.
3.trade: A carrier inside the ring is the tell for a wider war.

4.plain: One act awaits Sam's tick and got firmer a fifth time: Riyadh confirmed the East-West pipeline hit, Baghdad named Maysan, sacked the commander, shut the crossings, agreed a joint investigation with Tehran and has now found the launch platforms at al-Tib — a Gulf energy hit by an Iranian proxy, rung 7 by the rules; Tehran's wire still says nothing about it; the Khasab vessels (rung 5) are unnamed ~71 hours on; no fire on US forces since Sep 8, and CENTCOM's only word since is a blockade tally.
4.trade: A confirmed pipeline hit is the rung-7 print that re-prices Brent; watch for a rung-9 act (a US warship actually hit) or the first rung-10 act since February.

5.plain: Most likely next 14 days: Iran seizes or fires on a tanker; a Gulf energy strike is the second card; the Oman MOU track is the third — and two held signals (the UAE crown prince's meeting, Bahrain's refusal) would move the deal card up and the widen-the-war card up respectively if ticked.
5.trade: Tanker rates and war-risk premia up; XLE over SPX; long-dated Brent calls cheap if force-scenario odds are right.

6.plain: Iran wants to force an escalation before Nov 3; the US wants to squeeze and hold.
6.trade: No deal premium: fade rallies on 'talks' headlines unless a convoy actually transits.

7.plain: America's quiet bill: gas, yields, rial.
7.trade: DXY firm short-term (safe haven), soft long-term (reserve share).

8.plain: Iran and the small Gulf states pay; Israel doesn't.
8.trade: Qatar and Kuwait sovereign spreads wider; Israeli equities unaffected.

9.plain: Russia and Egypt win; Asia's importers lose; creditors trim.
9.trade: Long RUB oil revenue proxies; short INR/JPY on oil-import stress.

10.plain: The engine (lobby, arms, oil) still beats the brake (voters) — but the gap is closing.
10.trade: LMT/RTX hold while engine ≥8; first brake-over-engine print is the sell signal.

11.plain: Bigger war 33%, Stuck 31%, Strait regime 17%, Signed deal 8%, Regime change 6%.
11.trade: Bigger-war above 30% is the level to hedge with long-dated Brent calls; Signed deal above 20% is the level for Brent < $85.

12.plain: Weak signals: who sits at Monday's Muscat table after Bahrain's four conditions (Kuwait? Riyadh? Iraq, now invited?) and whether it is a briefing, a meeting or a signing — Reuters says no signature and Tehran still wants the fee; what Abu Dhabi says came out of the crown prince's meeting; Washington's first word on the table; a militia name from the launchers at al-Tib; Tehran's first word on the pipeline; the Houthi 'fully close Bab al-Mandeb' threat; two USAF tankers over the UAE on a Saturday night; Petroline; the Khasab identities; Monday's oil open; Wednesday's Fed; the Sep 26 panel fight; Pickaxe.

tiles.counter: one scale for every pot: 100° = boils over (a side gives up its aim); 80° = the emergency valve, past which a side is forced to escalate and acts against its own interest. Underneath, every pot shares one trigger on the 0–10 score — 7.0, the valve (re-fit monthly, the same for all four); the display maps 7.0 to 80° and 10 to 100°, so a degree means the same thing in every pot and the gap from 80° to 100° is a side's remaining tolerance

tiles.counter: definitions: Stuck = no signed deal, no regime change, door under 30 ships/day, fighting continues; Signed deal = a signed US–Iran agreement (not an MOU, not a pause); Regime change = any leadership change in Tehran, including an IRGC takeover or Khamenei succession; Bigger war = US or Israeli strikes on Iranian territory sustained over a week, or a Gulf-wide exchange, or US ground forces engaged; Strait regime = passage resumes ≥30 ships/day under Iran–Oman rules or fees, no war, no signed deal; Other = anything else (Houthi Red Sea closure, US unilateral pause, etc.)

tiles.source: Federal Reserve H.4.1, memorandum item: marketable Treasury securities held in custody for foreign official and international accounts (FRED WMTSECL1), Wednesday level, published Thursday 16:30 ET. Weekly since Apr 29 2026.
tiles.counter: Covers official accounts only (central banks, sovereign funds), not hedge funds or UK banks, and only what is custodied at the New York Fed — a central bank moving paper to Euroclear shows as a sale here without selling. It is a market-value level, so yields move it too. No public source gives daily per-country holdings; this is the closest weekly proxy.
tiles.moves: Every Thursday evening: append the new Wednesday level (the 19:00 run); a weekly drop above $30B is the alert line; cross-check with Japan MoF weekly securities flows (Thursday) when available

tiles.counter: AIS shows only ships that broadcast — dark tankers and most warships are invisible; ADS-B shows only aircraft with transponders on — military aircraft over Iran do not broadcast, so an empty sky is 'not seen', not 'not there'. Dead-reckoned positions are extrapolations, not fixes. Thermal anomalies cannot say what burned or who lit it
tiles.source: Live layer: every AIS commercial ship from hormuz.data-tracking.net /api/ships (MarineTraffic feeds, 30-min polls) and every ADS-B aircraft from adsb.lol (four 250-nm circles) — rebuilt every 10 minutes by a GitHub Action (live.json) and, between fixes, moved along last course and speed (dead reckoning, ≤20 min). Basemap: NASA VIIRS true colour via GIBS, newest complete pass (date on the toggle). Fire dots: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies, last 48 h (flares are normal; a new dot at a port, refinery or base is the signal). US warship positions: USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker (weekly, Monday) — the tracker names the sea, the point inside it is ours (JUDGMENT); roster as of Sep 8: George Washington + George H.W. Bush CSGs and the Boxer ARG in the Arabian Sea, Lincoln departed for Thailand Sep 2 · Satellite checks (S badges): Sentinel-2 via GIBS, 30 m, latest cloud-free pass per site, vessel counts at pier/anchor are our reading (JUDGMENT)

Scoreboard = latest official prints, not forecasts: Rosstat Q2 GDP (Aug 12), Bank of Russia balance of payments (Jan–May goods surplus, Q2 current account), MinFin monthly oil & gas revenue and H1 deficit; China NBS Q2 GDP / Jul activity / PPI-CPI (Aug 17) and General Administration of Customs August trade (Sep 8); Korea MOTIE August trade (Sep 1), Bank of Korea Q2 advance GDP and GDI, KRX H1 operating profit, SK hynix 2Q26; Brazil IBGE Q2 GDP, MDIC monthly trade, BCB Focus survey; Malaysia DOSM July trade (Aug 20), MITI, IMF WEO Jul 2026 for the growth forecast. Export-engine bars: same customs/ministry releases; Russia surplus = Jan–May monthly average; ringgit at 4.2 RM/$.
tiles.counter: These are correlations with the war window, not attributions: Korea and Malaysia are riding the AI-chip cycle, China's record exports are partly tariff front-running and a weak yuan, Brazil's crude surge started before March. Russia's beat is Q2 y/y against a weak 2025 base and its budget oil take is still falling. Most trade prints are one month; Q2 GDP is preliminary and gets revised.
tiles.moves: Monthly: China customs (~7th), Korea MOTIE (1st), Brazil MDIC (1st week), Malaysia DOSM (~20th), Russian MinFin oil & gas revenue (3rd). Quarterly: Q3 GDP prints late Oct (Korea, China) and Nov (Russia, Brazil). IMF October WEO replaces the July forecast column.
tiles.trade: The trade is not Russia or China — it is the AI-hardware exporters (Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan) and non-Gulf crude exporters (Brazil) that carry a war premium without war exposure; China gets export volume but no domestic lift; Russia gets prices and a current-account cushion but not budget cash.
